finding_resolutions.explanation: Added an owner-controlled attack-state reset acceptance criterion (plus matching validation requirement) to melee-enemy, ranged-enemy, and locked-door-enemy-attack, and added depends_on edges from floor-run-restart-persistent-closure to all three so full restart closure cannot complete while any archetype's in-progress attack (windup/in-flight shot/door-attack attempt) still carries over. enemy-pursuit-search-foundation's notes already establish that archetype-specific attack behavior belongs on the archetype items, so ownership is assigned there rather than widening the foundation's reset criterion.

Added an acceptance criterion and matching validation requirement to enemy-health-damage-defeat stating the defeat transition ends the enemy's participation as an active threat (pursuit/attack stops and it leaves play) while remaining the same persistent object restorable via the reset entry point, per GDD §1 Executive Summary and §3 Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission.

Added an acceptance criterion and matching validation requirement to enemy-health-damage-defeat that a persistent enemy's health/defeat state changes only through the owner-controlled damage interface and the floor-restart reset entry point, never on room transition, target loss, search, or doorway crossing, per GDD §5 Runtime Implementation and the Lower Vault/Door and Pursuit Rules persistent-pursuer premise.

Same underlying requirement as ES-F2 (defeated enemies stop being active threats). Resolved by the acceptance criterion added to enemy-health-damage-defeat; no separate work item is needed since this is behavior owned by that existing implementation item.

Cross-space persistence for pursuit state and active-enemy bookkeeping were already represented on enemy-pursuit-search-foundation and active-enemy-registry; the missing enemy-health half is resolved by the acceptance criterion added under ES-F3 to enemy-health-damage-defeat, completing the requirement's representation.

Same underlying requirement as ES-F1 (enemy attack state as a named restart participant with an owner-exposed reset entry point). Resolved by the attack-state reset acceptance criteria added to melee-enemy, ranged-enemy, and locked-door-enemy-attack plus the new depends_on edges from floor-run-restart-persistent-closure.

result.reasoning: All six supplied findings converge on two gaps in the enemy_state domain, both credibly supported by the GDD's restart-ownership and executive-summary/registry sections: (1) enemy attack-state (melee windup, ranged telegraphed shot/projectile, in-progress locked-door attack) had no owner-controlled reset entry point and was absent from floor-run-restart-persistent-closure's dependency closure, despite being a named required restart participant and despite enemy-pursuit-search-foundation's own notes disclaiming ownership of archetype-specific attack behavior; and (2) enemy-health-damage-defeat's acceptance surface covered the damage interface, one-shot defeat transition, and registry unregister call, but never obliged the defeated enemy to actually stop acting as a threat, nor obliged its health/defeat state to persist unchanged across room transitions (only registry/pursuit persistence were previously represented). I resolved both gaps with minimal, owner-appropriate acceptance/validation criterion additions plus three new dependency edges from floor-run-restart-persistent-closure to the three archetype/behavior items (all valid implementation-kind targets, no feature-target edges introduced, no cycles). The two deterministic REQ-ES-04/16/26 findings are the same underlying requirements surfaced by the deterministic checker and are resolved by the same corrections rather than duplicated work. I did not extend unresolved question #4, since that question concerns only how pursuit/search vs. status/displacement reset is split across two shared-state components; attack-state ownership is now unambiguous (each archetype owns and resets its own attack state), so no new ambiguity needs to be recorded there. No new work items, no scope invention, and no changes to sources/summary/seed_assessment were needed for this stream.
